title: A GitHub profile that updates itself

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Most people's GitHub profile is a static page. Antoine's refreshes on its own.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How? It's a repository, and its README is the profile. Ordinary Markdown, images, and a few embedded widgets.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So there's a server behind it somewhere?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, and that's the neat part. There's no application server at all. Scheduled updates run an automated workflow that renders fresh SVG images and metrics, and the README simply displays them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the profile is basically a small publishing pipeline.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Write once, let the schedule keep the visuals current. It's released under the GPL three license.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A simple idea, and it means the front page of his GitHub never goes stale. The full write-up has the details.
